title: iTrace: verification-first webcam eye-movement analysis
description: # iTrace manuscript revision, 2026-10-16 This deposit archives the corrected 30-page manuscript from reviewed commit `310be17ace8ae61621afe01329356427a3e6c861`. Exact source and figure artifacts are at https://github.com/docxology/itrace/tree/310be17ace8ae61621afe01329356427a3e6c861. It is a manuscript revision after the immutable v0.5.0 release, not a new package release. The package version in that source remains 0.5.0. The previous release remains at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23403300. References in the manuscript to that DOI identify the archived baseline. Changes correct overlap scoring, resampling and fit uncertainty, fitted-null diagnostics, uncertainty figures, scholarship, and scientific interpretation. The manuscript distinguishes synthetic verification from real-device validation. No new participant or reference-device data are claimed. Verification: 737 tests passed, 2 skipped, 91.05% combined statement-and-branch coverage; 44 final artifact tests passed, independent review approved the exact source commit, and all ten hosted CI jobs passed. The included figure manifest inventories 41 artifacts in the linked source tree. `provenance.json` binds this PDF to the Git commit; `SHA256SUMS` inventories every payload.
release_name: iTrace v0.5.0 (package baseline; corrected manuscript archived separately)

methods.name: Hardware-decoupled analysis core
methods.description: The optional capture shell emits typed records consumed by a headless scientific-analysis core.
methods.evidence: the shell may import the core, the core may never import the shell.

methods.name: Constructed-ground-truth verification
methods.description: Headless tests exercise the algorithms on synthetic signals whose truth is supplied by construction.
methods.evidence: its algorithms are exercised headlessly against constructed ground truth rather than camera availability.

methods.name: Explicit caller-supplied benchmark truth
methods.description: Benchmark outputs report their truth boundary and distinguish comparator agreement from reference measurement.
methods.evidence: every payload records the truth boundary instead of implying that detector agreement is a reference measurement.

key_findings: In the specified synthetic landmark-noise sweep, gaze remains below 2 deg RMS to sigma approximately 0.0048, about 3 pixels at 640-pixel width.
One-to-one overlap-based saccade recovery falls below F1 = 0.8 near sigma 0.0014, about 0.92 pixels, in that synthetic sweep.
The overlap result measures event recovery and does not establish timing accuracy.
Pupil noise-sweep robustness is conditional on the assumed pupil-noise injection model.
These results verify specified algorithms and internal geometry; they do not validate webcams as eye trackers.
key_findings_evidence: gaze remains below a 2 deg RMS bound to sigma approximately 0.0048 (about 3 px at 640 px width)
one-to-one overlap-based saccade recovery falls below F1 = 0.8 near sigma 0.0014 (about 0.92 px).
This is event recovery, not a timing-accuracy measurement.
The pupil channel is reported conditionally because its noise-sweep robustness follows from the modelling assumption used to inject pupil noise.
Its contribution is not a claim that webcams are validated eye trackers;
